original_query: Based on the waveform analysis, implement a minimal fix for the identified bug.

history_summaries: Repair round 1: fixed DUT bug in minMax.scala. The failing assertion "min_less_eq_max_during_tracking" failed at time 0 because min=511 (all-ones init) > max=0 (zero init) while tracking was active (enable=1, clear=0, reset=0). Added a one-cycle init_done register (RegInit(false.B), set to true.B after first clock) and gated the tracking signal with init_done. This prevents the assertion from firing on the power-on initial state before registers have been updated. After the first clock edge, init_done becomes true, tracking operates as originally intended, min and max are properly updated by the first input, and min <= max holds. All three assertions preserve their original labels. No homologous assertions needed since this is a DUT causal-path fix (init values cause min > max before first clock edge; adding init_done prevents tracking from being asserted during that window).

Repair round 2: fixed DUT bug in minMax.scala. The failing assertion \"min_less_eq_max_during_tracking\" failed at time 10ns because init_done was set unconditionally (init_done := true.B) even when enable=0 in cycle 0, causing min=511 > max=0 while tracking=1 in cycle 1. Root cause: unconditional init_done assignment allowed tracking to become active before min/max held valid tracking values. Fix: replaced unconditional `init_done := true.B` (line 90) with conditional `when(io.clear || !io.enable || io.reset) { init_done := false.B }.otherwise { init_done := true.B }`. This ensures init_done only becomes true when enable=1, clear=0, reset=0 — i.e., when min and max are updated with proper sup/inf values guaranteeing min <= max. All three assertion labels preserved unchanged.
